    Search changeset comments

    Source: R/osmapi_changeset_discussion.R
    osm_search_comment_changeset_discussion.Rd

    Returns changeset comments that match the specified query. If no query is provided, the most recent changeset comments are returned.

    Usage

    osm_search_comment_changeset_discussion(
  user,
  from,
  to,
  format = c("R", "xml", "json"),
  tags_in_columns = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    user

    Search for changeset comments created by the user with the given user id (numeric) or display name (character).

    from

    Beginning date range. See details for the valid formats.

    to

    End date range. Only works when from is supplied. See details for the valid formats.

    format

    Format of the output. Can be "R" (default), "xml", or "json".

    tags_in_columns

    If FALSE (default), the tags of the changesets are saved in a single list column tags containing a data.frame for each changeset with the keys and values. If TRUE, add a column for each key. Ignored if format != "R".

    Value

    If format = "R", returns a data frame with one comment per If format = "xml", returns a xml2::xml_document. If format = "json", returns a list with the json structure.

    Details

    The valid formats for from and to parameters are POSIXt values or characters preferably in ISO 8601 format.

    See also

    Other changeset discussion's functions: osm_comment_changeset_discussion(), osm_hide_comment_changeset_discussion(), osm_subscribe_changeset_discussion()

    Examples

    # See the latest changeset comments globally:
osm_search_comment_changeset_discussion()

#> 8   Yes, typically parking lots, driveways, even access roads into and throughout industrial properties are not maintained by local city, parish, or state. However, they are mapped and tagged with tags such as highway=service, and depending on additional specific uses, they could be tagged with service=parking_aisle, service=driveway, etc. These roads typically do not have a name=*, as they are not officially named - with some exceptions. I highly recommend reading the highway=* and highway=service wiki pages, which you can get to by clicking the tag in this comment, it's a highlighted link. An excerpt from the highway=service page states:\n\n"The highway=service tag denotes ways used for vehicle access to a building, parking lot, service station, business estate, beach, campsite, etc. Service ways are usually not part of the public street network and may sometimes be inaccessible to the general public"\n\nGovernment maintained highways are normally tagged with highway=motorway, highway=primary, highway=secondary, highway=tertiary, highway=unclassified, highway=residential, and many other highway=* tags, typically with a name=* tag.\n\nThe term "highway" may be confusing, but that is why we define what sort of highway it is, the roads you deleted were tagged with highway=service. \n\nI understand the pain of turning into a spot with an almost impossibly navigable area in a semi cab hauling about 60' worth of space for equipment to deliver the load (rollback + double car hauler trailer), but ultimately this should be on the driver to check via maps or survey in person before attempting to turn into an unfamiliar area. If there are truly no trucks permitted entry, with signage that states no thru trucks, or no trucks in general, the highway=* way may be tagged with hgv=no, signifying that heavy goods vehicles (semis, essentially, basic OpenStreetMap tags are made with European terms in mind) are not permitted on that highway=* way.

I felt I had to send a message before I went to bed though, because I maintain a feed of changes in Wales and you were making more changesets than people do in the span on a month so my feed was basically just you (which was quite amusing to be fair).\n\nDon't worry, your changes are much appreciated, and addresses and access are quite common and important issues to resolve. In general, adding the address to the house, and including the path to the house (with `access=private`, you don't have to specify specific modes of transport since this is implied), should be sufficient. If you want to map the entrance you can do that as well, but it should be a node on the building tagged as `entrance=main`. The entrance itself doesn't need address tags (unless the address differs from the rest of the building, e.g. for terraces) since that is implied by the building.\n\nSetting `access=no` will prevent any software from ever routing to it, including delivery drivers etc, since that implies they can't go down that road even with the permission of the owner. Settings the paths to `access=private` will help with that.\n\nI assume both of the speed limits on the roads were added by accident?\n\nThank you for responding :)
